highlights.summary: John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips. Invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang ’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most…
body: The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was put at risk by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.
Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s CEO on 12 November after allegations surfaced of extramarital relationships with the suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, had been executive director of Megaspeed International. Megaspeed facilitated about $12bn in chip sales, in violation of export controls in the US, where the Trump administration has prohibited the selling of advanced AI chips to China.
On Sunday’s edition of CNN’s State of the Union, the Trump administration’s national intelligence director, Jay Clayton, said he suspected China was able to obtain Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips.

highlights.title: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
highlights.summary: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the vibe-hacking of everything, follow David Pierce. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started.
body: Large language models can now redesign your TV and upgrade your camera for you. Is the physical world ready to be Claude Code-d?

Like so many things with AI, it’s not that large language models opened up some wholly new capability. For as long as there have been gadgets, a few users have been hacking, modding, jailbreaking, and tweaking them to their liking. What is new is that it’s easy now. People all over the world are discovering that they can use large language models to hack their hardware simply by prompting Claude Code or Codex to do it. It has led to a boom in developer-friendly gadgets and created a market for better software on just about every device you can think of.

highlights.title: Sorry, Vice City, but You’re the Most Boring Part of GTA 6
highlights.summary: When Grand Theft Auto 6 was first announced, fans were thrilled at the prospect of returning to Vice City. The Miami-inspired location has always been one of the series’ most memorable locations, its neon-lit streets standing in contrast to the grittiness of Liberty City.
body: I don’t mean to say that Vice City sucks — far from it! It’s an immaculately designed video game city with more environmental diversity in any given corner than some open-world games fit into an entire map. The fact that it’s one of my least favorite places to spend time is more a testament to every other location in GTA 6 ’s Florida-inspired world. From small towns to the deep wilderness, every corner of Leonida is a delight to discover because every area feels so different.

Even after getting out of the Leonida Keys, it’s still a while before you get to Vice City. First, Jason and Lucia spend a stint upstate hopping around some small towns separated by vast farmland. Port Gellhorn has the feel of an industrial town, the kind of place that’s lined with used car lots. Some great action set pieces come out of that setup; one time I busted up a well-guarded abandoned bowling alley and wound up in a gritty gang shootout.

body: Huelva’s prizes highlight the festival’s focus under director Manuel H. Martín on crossover films, often mixing genre-bending and social issues to surprising effect. Top winner “After Elena.” from Chile’s Shawn Garry, turns on mourning but is a comedy; Lucía Puenzo’s “Pepita, the Gunslinger” is a gangster movie but the gangster is a woman who battles corruption. “Funk,” which won Duda Santos best actress, is a musical but “revolutionary,” says director Aly Muritiba, in its centering “Black joy.”
The 2026 awards also may be the gayest in Huelva’s history, with nearly half going to LGBT movies in a year where Variety has asked whether the 2026-27 Oscars season is their gayest ever.

The double nods for the Shawn Garry directed “After Elena”(“Después de Elena”) also underscore what Huelva does best: Highlighting titles that deserve further recognition which in the case of Latin America includes most of its movies, given they are under-covered by the international media.

highlights.title: An age gap isn’t always a problem, partner abuse is | Letters
highlights.summary: Readers respond to articles on relationships and the age of consent. Regarding Polly Hudson’s article ( At 17, I dated a 36-year-old. That decision looks very different to me now, 15 November ), I met and lived with a 35-year-old man when I was 17.
body: I learned that he had done it all before, pursuing schoolgirls. I tried to break free multiple times, only to find that he had phoned my new partner, or read my diary so he could block my plans. This is about having control, it is not just a sexual preference.

The men doing this are rarely satisfied, and criticism can escalate to coercive, emotionally abusive levels. In some cases (though not in mine) girls are pimped out, shared with the man’s friends, imprisoned against their will.

Polly Hudson should not be angry with her younger self. Would she be angry with another young girl who found herself in similar circumstances? Unlikely. There is something else that has stopped us speaking out: fear. Fear of physical or verbal retaliation by the perpetrator; of the judgment of those around us; of a legal system that fails to punish abusers and shames victims with hackneyed tropes that have long been disproven; of public and private organisations that continue to bury abuse allegations and enable perpetrators who bring in cash, clicks, viewers or shareholders.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
highlights.summary: To establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how to measure speed.
body: A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity.

Slowing AI development became a particularly hot topic after a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher said the companies were “gambling with our lives,” and even Anthropic’s IPO filing suggested that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to society.”

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Among other things, Amodei called for companies to agree to “common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.”

But to establish a speed limit on AI development, you need an agreed-upon measurement for speed. Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name ) could be that measurement.

highlights.title: I covered myself in sleep trackers to find the very best
highlights.summary: Get a better night’s sleep with monitoring and guidance from smartwatches, smart rings, smart bands and sleep earbuds. The best sleep masks and best Bluetooth sleep masks. Getting quality sleep is just as crucial as getting enough sleep. And how you feel in the morning only tells part of the story.
body: Armed with this information, you can learn how your lifestyle affects your sleep. Maybe your after dinner cappuccino triggers a night of tossing and turning, or you’re more restful after evening workouts. As the wise GI Joe once said, knowing is half the battle. And the more you know about your sleep, the better chance you have of improving it.

As a consumer technology journalist for more than two decades, I began wearing fitness trackers in the early 2010s and have since reviewed hundreds of products in the sleep and fitness space. After spending more than 15 years tracking my sleep nightly, I have a deep understanding of how wearables work, which brands and products are reliable and how to best interpret app data.

I wore up to five wearables at a time (two wrist devices, two rings, and earbuds) for at least seven nights each. Every morning, I plotted sleep data into a spreadsheet, including duration, sleep stages (light, REM, deep, awake), along with average sleep heart rate and heart rate variability (HRV) when available.

In Rockstar's official promotional materials for the game, both Jason and Lucia were prominently featured wearing stylish clothing, from Lucia's body-hugging gold dress to Jason's slick Miami Vice -inspired aqua sport…
body: Having a diverse wardrobe isn't just a fun little customization touch in GTA 6. If you're reported for committing a crime in Leonida — and this will happen very often — police will be able to recognize you based on your car, your physical appearance, and what you're wearing. Keeping a couple spare outfits in your trunk or hastily buying a new ensemble on the run can be the difference between a successful job and ending up busted (or wasted).

I'm taking my time with GTA 6 and still kicking around the introductory area of Key Lento. I know I should be putting money in my family savings account. It would probably be in my best interest to learn how to drive without sideswiping semi-trucks or taking out stop signs. Perhaps I ought to be buying more guns. Instead, I'm trawling South Leonida for all the vintage and souvenir shops I can find. You can keep your fancy cars. I've got a T-shirt collection to maintain.

body: AI cheating has become a growing controversy in Clash Royale, with increasingly sophisticated bots reportedly capable of outperforming skilled human players. Players highlighted claims that an AI-controlled account named ‘Clasher’ had reached the top of the game’s global leaderboard.

The situation prompted calls for Supercell to intervene, with the developer addressing the controversy on November 20. In a statement posted on X, Clash Royale warned that using AI or other tools to cheat was a “royal crime,” declaring that offending players would be banished from the Arena.
On November 21, the official Clash Royale X account announced that it had caught the creator of an AI cheating tool and recruited them to help develop new anti-cheat technology.

“The creator of the AI cheating tool has been caught,” Supercell announced in a statement framed as a royal decree from the King. “He’s agreed, entirely of his own free will, to join forces with the Clash Royale team.

highlights.title: The link between nurturing and masculinity | Letter
highlights.summary: Clincal psychotherapist Gareth Strangemore-Jones responds to an article on persistent assumptions about masculinity. Sarah Blaffer Hrdy’s research offers an important challenge to one of our most persistent assumptions about masculinity: that nurturing is somehow contrary to male nature ( Would…
body: We often imagine psychological development as a process in which attitudes must change before behaviour follows. Yet caregiving may work in both directions. Repeated experiences of responding to another person’s vulnerability can engage and potentially strengthen the biological and psychological systems involved in emotional responsiveness, attachment and cooperation.

But we should be cautious about extending this into the claim that more nurturing fathers would necessarily produce a more peaceful world. Human beings are capable of extraordinary tenderness towards their own children while remaining hostile towards those outside their immediate circle. Empathy can be selective, and the causes of collective violence extend far beyond individual temperament.
Perhaps the more important question is whether the emotional capacities developed through caregiving can be extended towards strangers, communities and people with whom we disagree.

highlights.title: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash
highlights.summary: Journalist Paris Marx unpacks his new book "Hyperscale."
body: In his new book “Hyperscale,” journalist Paris Marx investigates the impact of data centers and generative AI, taking readers inside the data centers themselves and explaining how computing infrastructure that goes back decades recently became a political landmine.

The book is well-timed, to put it mildly, as data center backlash seems to have been one of the motivators for the massive blue wave seen in the recent midterm elections. And those debates are likely to continue as Democrats wield more governmental power.

In an interview with TechCrunch, Marx described the data center buildout as “fundamentally unsustainable” and “completely out of line with a livable planet,” while also arguing that these facilities make for an obvious target amidst broader anger at the tech industry. After all, if a data center is being built in your community, “it’s very physical, it’s very material.”

highlights.title: Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds
highlights.summary: Transparency International says Queensland’s David Crisafulli was ‘by far the most frequently accessed’ state leader, with 13 meetings. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: Bosses at 10 datacentre companies secured almost 120 meetings with premiers and ministers in five states over a three-year period, with experts declaring this is “just the tip of the iceberg”.

Analysis by Transparency International Australia argues these meetings, when combined with political donations, demonstrate “unfettered access” to decision-makers that creates an “uneven playing field”.

The report found donations from major datacentre companies and their contracted lobbying firms nearly tripled over the past three years from $685,000 to $1.8m, coinciding with increased investment across Australia.

The analysis found the Queensland leader, David Crisafulli, was “by far the most frequently accessed state premier”, with public diaries showing he has met datacentre executives 13 times in the past three years.

highlights.title: How to steal the BF Bandito in GTA 6
highlights.summary: You need to find a way to steal the BF Bandito in Grand Theft Auto 6 to help out Moses. After completing the first batch of requests, Moses will contact you about other cars he wants you to retrieve for him. Among them is this off-road beast.
body: You will find the BF Bandito moving around the northern part of Buckskin Swamp, on the southeastern side of Kelly County. As you approach the area, you will see a few cars and motorcycles driving around an off-road circuit. The BF Bandito is a white vehicle that's always followed by a motorcycle riding alongside it. You can also check the gallery to see a picture of it.

The challenge when it comes to stealing this car is that you need to make its driver stop so you can get them out and drive it back to Moses. The best strategy here is to simply block its path, which you can do by parking a car in the middle of the track where the vehicles are racing. If you aren't driving a large car when running this mission, don't worry. You can find a pickup truck at the intersection on the east side of the area.

Once the driver stops the BF Bandito, you can steal it. Since they were already driving it, you won't need to break in or hotwire it. We do advise dealing with the person on the motorcycle, as they will shoot at you and pursue you after you take the car.

body: So much of Alcaraz’s fortunes this season were defined by the wrist injury that forced him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer. No matter, he still managed to tick the two most important items off his to-do list this year.

After starting 2026 by becoming the youngest man in history to earn the career grand slam, he is now, at 23, the fourth man to win all four grand slams and the ATP Finals. Despite his long absence, he has missed only two of the four majors and two of the nine Masters 1000 events: the Canadian Open and Shanghai Masters.

Faster indoor courts were previously viewed as the conditions that make Alcaraz most vulnerable. It is fair to say that this is no longer true. Alcaraz ends his year on a 14-match winning streak after triumphing on two of the fastest courts, Paris and Turin.

highlights.summary: Though his career has spanned over four decades, John Turturro still feels like it’s just the beginning. body: “I am a very fortunate person to make a good living as an actor, sometimes as a writer, a director, doing something that I deeply love. To put all of yourself into what you do and give a piece of that away in your work is something that I learned from my parents,” Turturro said. “They taught me that a job well done defines who you are. Building a house, making a dress was done brick by brick, stitch by stitch.”
He called filmmaking the “magic and beauty of life” and “an offering that you hope others will receive with open hearts.”

“A great writer, Cesare Pavese, once said that the only great thing in life is to begin. And I still consider myself a beginner in many ways,” he concluded. “For me, when I do a job, every job is like a first love. And I consider this award an encouragement to continue to try.”

highlights.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
highlights.summary: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
body: A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model. Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “ an alien mind ⁠ ”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation.

The primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking the perplexity of the models on a held-out dataset. 2, 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions. The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5.

highlights.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
highlights.summary: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge says it took six weeks for him using the AI tool to solve 19th-century Riemann hypothesis. A mathematician at Anthropic has said that the San Francisco -based artificial intelligence (AI) company’s software has helped crack one of the most important unsolved problems in…
body: Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.
On Saturday afternoon, two organizations announced that they had independently verified Alpöge’s claim after reviewing the programming language he used to share the solution.

The proof evidently marks another breakthrough in the use of AI for complicated math problems – even as mathematicians express uneasiness around extremely lucrative private companies dishing out millions of dollars for the technology to solve problems.

“Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line,” Alpöge wrote, while anthropomorphizing the AI software. “No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”

highlights.title: Thitikul completes three-peat at LPGA Tour finale and breaks money record
highlights.summary: Jeeno Thitikul has won the LPGA Tour's season-ending CME Group Tour Championship for a third consecutive year after storming to a two-shot victory in Florida.
body: Thitikul carded an eagle and five birdies during an impressive seven-under 65, pulling her clear of a congested leaderboard at Tiburon Golf Club and securing a 12th LPGA Tour title.
She finished on 24 under and two clear of Aki Iwai, who raced into contention with six birdies in the first 10 holes of her final-round 65, while world No 1 Nelly Korda finished in third spot.

Thitikul becomes the first player to win an LPGA Tour event three years running since Inbee Park at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship from 2013-2015, with her latest a fifth of another memorable season.
A $4m (£3.06m) first prize also sees her end Annika Sorenstam's 25-year stint at the top of the LPGA Tour's career money list, moving ahead of the Swede with a total of $24,292,858 (£20.3m).

highlights.summary: The gaming industry is notoriously secretive, and that's doubly true for anything related to Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar Games kept much of the game tightly under wraps, including one of the title's biggest secrets — a remarkable feat when you consider how much of the game leaked prior to launch.
body: Amber Wallin is a comedian who voices several non-playable characters in GTA 6. Wallin's voice can be heard during an early segment of the game where Lucia is notified she will be allowed to carry out her sentence via a quasi-home arrest program. Wallin appears in a few other roles throughout the game, such as a character who roasts Jason after he harasses her.
Given her profession, it's no surprise that Wallin's characters are a hoot. "Motherfucker wanna clock out soon when shit gets real," she says via the aggravated NPC. "Clock in, ho. Time is money!"

While Wallin's various roles are minor, the game is already the biggest entertainment launch of all time, meaning anyone who can say they were involved in its creation has much to brag about. So, imagine the surprise of Wallin's husband when he learned she was in the game like any other player. According to a video the couple recently posted on social media, Wallin apparently kept her involvement in the game a total secret from even her husband for two years.

highlights.title: Delta flights in and out of Atlanta delayed due to system outage
highlights.summary: All Delta flights in and out of Atlanta are facing significant delays on Sunday due to a problem with the system that calculates a plane's weight and balance. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is Delta's largest hub and one of the busiest airports in the world.
body: Major delays for Delta come just a week after a nationwide groundstop.

The system that went offline calculates the total weight of an airplane, including its airframe, fuel, passengers and their baggage. The system also allows pilots to determine the plane’s center of gravity and whether the weight is evenly distributed — data points that help ensure safe passage.
“Delta teams are using manual workarounds this morning to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation,” the airline said in a statement on Sunday.

highlights.title: The UN fails to agree on rules regulating ‘killer robots’
highlights.summary: One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called "killer robots." Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to "start discussing options" after a largely fruitless week of…
body: Before the negotiations got underway, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the guardian of the Geneva Conventions, said it was urgent for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. That call was backed by the U.N. secretary-general and by Pope Leo.

The compromise reached was that countries would instead have two years to propose regulations. Negotiations between countries on which regulations to adopt and how to enforce them will likely drag on well beyond that. Additionally, room was left for some of those yet-to-be-adopted regulations to remain “optional.”

Humanitarian organizations and some countries see a need to urgently adopt legally binding rules as semi-autonomous weapons and drones have been responsible for a significant number of civilian deaths in conflicts around the globe, including in Ukraine, Gaza, and Sudan.
On day one, Russia delayed proceedings by objecting to the meeting’s agenda. Then the United States proposed a five-year window to discuss nonbinding, optional guidelines for autonomous weapons.

highlights.title: Rockstar Says Jason's Viral Personality in GTA 6 Comes From Steve McQueen and Real-Life Veterans
highlights.summary: Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life. As 13 years of waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto ended last week, players have found themselves enamored with Jason Duval.
body: The studio's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, talked about how the studio behind the mega-hit video game built Jason from the ground up during a conversation with Destructoid. Centering the story on a "couple on the run" marked new territory for Rockstar, but it's far from a new concept in entertainment. So, the team turned to movies, particularly Sam Peckinpah's The Getaway.

"Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries explained. "We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite."

He continued, saying that Rockstar's research into real-world veterans and Army Rangers helped refine its approach. Those who have played the game (and keen-eyed trailer watchers ) already know about Jason's military background, so the influence here definitely tracks.
"These guys typically aren’t running their mouths or reacting to something unless it’s strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves."

As 13 years of waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto ended last week, players have found themselves enamored with Jason Duval.

body: Creator Edmund McMillen claims he ‘had no idea’ AI music was used in the latest version of Binding of Isaac.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Creator Edmund McMillen took to X to apologize and claimed he “had no idea” the in-game GTA parody used generative AI music. Adding to the drama, Valve requires developers to disclose how and when they use generative AI in the development process, and Nicalis, Inc., the studio behind Repentance Plus, doesn’t appear to have mentioned the AI music anywhere.

Within hours of the discovery, Nicalis shared on X that Repentance Plus had been updated and the generated music files had been removed. highlights.title: Forget the Lighthouse, GTA 6’s Best Minigame Is a Full-Blown Zombie Shooter That Will Take You Hours To Beat
highlights.summary: Yes, we know you're all playing GTA 6, but don't forget to check out Street Trash 3: Dezombifier, the certified banger on Jason's JoySystem console.
body: To say I was up until midnight last night with GTA 6 is technically correct, but not the full picture. What I was actually doing was headshotting undead nightmares in Street Trash 3: Dezombifier, a moreish isometric twin-stick shooter that lives inside Jason's PS5-alike JoySystem.
You play it briefly with Cal during the story, and it impressed me enough to want to beat it fully. After nearly four hours, I still haven't.

It's clearly inspired by the Sony-published Dead Nation from 2010, but it mashes the zombie slaying with a roguelike deckbuilder. Every time an enemy squelches, their blood splattering the pavement, you gain XP, and at each new level you pick a card to adjust your build. Basic cards boost movement speed, fire rate, damage or critical hit chance, but rarer cards transform your tactics, such as one that doubles your damage given and received.

Your goal is to collect six gears strewn around a deceptively large map and leave via a rooftop chopper. You'll die a lot, but on each run you'll learn a little more about the world's layout and discover new cards to experiment with.
points: Yes, we know you're all playing GTA 6, but don't forget to check out Street Trash 3: Dezombifier, the certified banger on Jason's JoySystem console.
